llm.reply:
MLH1 (NCBIGene:4292) and MSH2 (NCBIGene:4436) are both mismatch repair genes implicated in hereditary colorectal cancer syndromes, but they map to distinct clinical entities [1][5]. MLH1 is associated with Muir-Torré syndrome, hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer type 2, and mismatch repair cancer syndrome 1 [2][3][4]. MSH2 is linked to Lynch syndrome 1 and mismatch repair cancer syndrome 2 [6][7].

## Gene Function and Biology

MLH1 encodes a protein that heterodimerizes with PMS2 to form MutL alpha, a core component of the DNA mismatch repair system that introduces single-strand breaks near DNA mismatches [18: "can heterodimerize with mismatch repair endonuclease PMS2 to form MutL alpha, part of the DNA mismatch repair system"]. Both genes participate in mismatch repair and meiotic mismatch repair biological processes [21][15][26]. MLH1 was identified as a locus frequently mutated in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer [18: "identified as a locus frequently mutated in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer"].

## ClinVar Variants and Functional Studies

Multiple ClinVar variants have been catalogued for MLH1, including NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.545+1271_677+737delinsCA, NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.453+625_545+920delinsT, NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.1418A>T (p.His473Leu), and NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.884+5T>A [10][17][23][28]. Functional assays have assessed variants of unknown significance in both MLH1 and MSH2 to identify patients with Lynch syndrome [22]. Additional studies have characterized MLH1-deficient colorectal carcinomas with promoter hypermethylation and KRAS mutations [16].

## Clinical Trials and Therapeutic Relevance

Several clinical trials target mismatch repair–deficient cancers relevant to MLH1 and MSH2, including a study of MK-3475 in patients with microsatellite unstable tumors and trials making genetic testing accessible for hereditary cancer risk [19][29][24][13]. Research on deficient mismatch repair colorectal cancer continues to characterize the clinicopathological and molecular features of these tumors [27].

MLH1 (NCBIGene:4292, mutL homolog 1) and MSH2 (NCBIGene:4436, mutS homolog 2) are both DNA mismatch repair genes implicated in hereditary colorectal cancer predisposition, but they associate with partially distinct syndrome spectra [1][3][5][6]. MLH1 is linked to Muir-Torre syndrome, hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer type 2, and mismatch repair cancer syndrome 1 [2][3][4]. MSH2 is linked to Lynch syndrome 1 and mismatch repair cancer syndrome 2 [6][7].

## Gene Function and Biology

MLH1 encodes a protein that heterodimerizes with PMS2 to form MutL alpha, which introduces single-strand breaks near DNA mismatches when bound by MutS beta, and can also heterodimerize with MLH3 to form MutL gamma involved in meiosis [18: "heterodimerize with mismatch repair endonuclease PMS2 to form MutL alpha"][18: "heterodimerize with DNA mismatch repair protein MLH3 to form MutL gamma"]. Both genes participate in mismatch repair (GO:0006298) and response to stress (GO:0006950), with MLH1 additionally involved in meiotic mismatch repair (GO:0000710) [21][26][15].

## Variant and Literature Evidence

Multiple ClinVar variants have been catalogued for MLH1, including NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.545+1271_677+737delinsCA, NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.453+625_545+920delinsT, NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.1418A>T (p.His473Leu), and NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.884+5T>A [10][17][23][28]. Functional analyses of MLH1 variants and methylation tolerance-based assays assessing variants of unknown significance in both MLH1 and MSH2 have been published to identify patients with Lynch syndrome [9][22]. MLH1-deficient colorectal carcinomas with promoter hypermethylation have been shown to harbor KRAS mutations and arise from conventional adenomas [16]. Clinicopathological and molecular characterization of deficient mismatch repair colorectal cancer has also been reported [27].

## Clinical Trials and Testing Access

Clinical trials relevant to genetic predisposition and mismatch repair deficiency include the IMPACT Study for prostate cancer predisposition, a pembrolizumab (MK-3475) study in microsatellite unstable tumors, surgical prevention of ovarian cancer in patients with genetic mutations, and the MAGENTA trial making genetic testing accessible [13][19][24][29]. Additional publications identified include PMID 17510385, PMID 27438990, PMID 30998989, and PMID 36150551 [14][20][25][30].
